entities.text: Commissioner Municipal Corporation ... vs Ku. Nikita Jatav Minor Thr. Her Natural
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
1 Appellant-Municipal Commissioner, Gwalior has filed this appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 assailing the impugned award dated 12/9/2019 passed by Seventh Member,
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior in MACC No. 1278/2017; whereby, the claim case filed by respondent No. 1 seeking a compensation of Rs. 5,50,000/- for the injuries sustained by her in road accident dated 12/8/2017 has been allowed in part and Claims Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs. 44,472/- with interest at the rate of 7% per annum and while exonerating the Insurance Company from the liability totally, directed the appellant and respondent No. 2 (driver)
to make the payment of compensation amount.
2.

From perusal of record as well as impugned award, it is apparent that Claims Tribunal exonerated the Insurance Company on the ground that on the date of accident, the offending vehicle was unregistered with the RTO.
It was purchased on 25/3/2017 and issued temporary registration for a month i.e. up to 24/4/2017.
Though the vehicle got insured on 25/4/2017; however, on the date of accident i.e. 12/8/2017 it was unregistered and after the accident, on 25/5/2018 it was got registered.

3. Since the vehicle was not validly registered, the complainant ought not to have used / plied the vehicle on road or use the same and by doing so, he has certainly violated Section 39 of The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 as well as terms and conditions of the insurance policy, thereby entitling the insurance company to repudiate the claim.

4. Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of United India Insurance Company Limited Vs. Sushil Kumar Godara(2021)14SCC519, repudiated the insurance claim on three grounds, one of which, was that the temporary registration of the vehicle expired on 19.07.2011 and the respondent (insured) did not get the vehicle permanently registered.

entities.text: United India Insurance Company Limited Vs. Sushil Kumar Godara(2021)14SCC519,
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appeal filed by the insurance company was allowed and the complaint filed by respondent (complainant) was dismissed.

It was also held that since the vehicle had been driven / used without a valid registration, it amounts to clear violation of Sections 39 and 192 of The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and has resulted in fundamental breach of the terms and conditions of the policy.

In the aforesaid case of United India Insurance Company Limited (supra), reliance was placed upon judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Narinder Singh Vs.
New India Assurance Company Limited and others, (2014)9SCC324, wherein the claim was in the context of an accident, involving a vehicle, the temporary registration of which had expired, Hon'ble Apex Court while dismissing the appeal preferred by owner held that the insurer was not liable for making payment of compensation amount.

entities.text:
Narinder Singh Vs.
New India Assurance Company Limited and others, (2014)9SCC324,
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. In view of aforesaid legal pronouncements, when indisputable, in the instant case a temporary registration so granted in respect of the vehicle in question, had expired on 24/4/2017 and alleged accident took placed on 12/8/2017 when the vehicle was without any registration, in the opinion of this Court, learned Claims Tribunal did not err in passing the impugned award thereby exonerating the Insurance Company from its liability.
6. No infirmity, illegality, irregularity or perversity has been committed by the learned Claims Tribunal while passing the impugned award.
Appeal sans merits and is hereby dismissed.
